headline: Sellers Hold the Upper Hand as Semis and Homebuilders Drag Mid-Session
body_html:
Wednesday's session is shaping up as a broadly defensive affair, with 394 stocks in our 544-name universe trading lower against just 144 in positive territory at midday. The selling is not uniform, but it is deep where it counts: Semiconductors are off 2.16% and Homebuilders have surrendered 2.43%, two of the market's most rate-sensitive corners, as investors brace ahead of the Federal Reserve's latest meeting minutes. Gold is retreating and the dollar is firming, a combination that tends to pressure risk assets and is doing exactly that across cyclicals today.

Healthcare is the lone relative sanctuary, down a modest 0.11% and providing the session's standout movers. Glaukos leads the entire universe with a 4.86% advance, while Addus HomeCare adds 3.27% and TransMedics Group tacks on 2.07%, giving the sector an unusual pocket of strength. Corteva is the surprise gainer in Agriculture, rising 3.39%, possibly catching a bid as Middle East tensions stoke commodity-supply concerns. On the opposite end, Worthington Steel is off 7.42%, pacing a bruising day for Materials, and Coherent drops 5.16% as optical-networking names retreat sharply.

Into the close, traders will be watching whether the Fed-minutes release sharpens or softens the rate narrative and whether Industrials, currently down 1.22%, find any footing. Thursday's open will carry whatever risk premium the geopolitical headlines settle at by tonight.

briefs.headline: Fed Minutes Loom as Gold Retreats and Dollar Firms
briefs.body: Investors are repositioning ahead of the Federal Reserve's release of its latest meeting minutes, with gold slipping and the dollar extending gains mid-session. The shift is drawing money out of rate-sensitive sectors and into cash-equivalent positions, amplifying selling pressure across Semiconductors and Homebuilders in particular.

briefs.headline: Shell Flags Record Refining Margins as Iran Tensions Lift Fuel Prices
briefs.body: Shell indicated it expects refining margins to reach record levels as conflict involving Iran tightens global fuel supply. The disclosure is lending modest support to the Energy sector, which is the second-best performer today, down only 0.17%, even as broader markets retreat.

briefs.headline: Escalating Yemen Fighting Rattles Gulf Markets and Commodities
briefs.body: Houthi forces attacked Aden airport as United Nations agencies reported more than 200,000 people displaced by renewed fighting. Turkey confirmed it is providing technical and defensive support to Saudi Arabia, while Gulf equity markets turned subdued. The unrest is adding a geopolitical risk premium to oil-supply assumptions.

briefs.headline: India Joins Global Rate-Tightening Cycle With First Hike in Four Years
briefs.body: India's central bank raised interest rates for the first time in nearly four years, aligning the country with a worldwide tightening wave. The move reinforces the higher-for-longer monetary narrative that is pressuring growth equities globally and contributing to mid-session weakness in rate-sensitive corners of the U.S. market.

briefs.headline: Google Ordered to Pause Two Data Centers in European Regulatory Action
briefs.body: A European authority has instructed Alphabet's Google to halt construction on two data centers in a jurisdiction regulators have likened to a tech-investment hub. The order adds to the regulatory overhang facing large technology infrastructure projects and is weighing on sentiment in the Software and networking segments today.

briefs.headline: UK Flooring Retailer Headlam to Delist After Insolvency Filing
briefs.body: British floor-coverings distributor Headlam will be removed from public markets after collapsing into administration. The failure resonates with weakness in domestic consumer and flooring names; Mohawk Industries, the U.S. flooring giant, is among today's steepest decliners, sliding 5.11% in the Consumer sector.
